Therefore, it is not surprising that the economic conflicts pointed out above most frequently involve water in one way or another. This may involve actual removal of the water or destruction of the source or changing the physical or chemical quality of the water. If endangered species are to be successfully restored, alternative sources of water will, in those instances, need to be developed.
In summary, the economic environment of endangered species restoration under the proposed legislation includes the direct values foregone or anticipated from the use of endangered species for trade products or sporting purposes, the costs of development of alternative resources to replace those sacrificed to protect endangered species habitats, and the benefits resulting from the recreational use of natural areas developed for the protection of endangered species.
